title: PLTSa Sentiment Analysis
subtitle: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis on Indonesian Twitter Discourse

desc.overview: Analyzing public sentiment toward Waste-to-Energy (PLTSa) initiatives in Indonesia using zero-shot Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis on Twitter discourse from January 2025 to May 2026.
desc.problem: PLTSa projects involve a complex balance between environmental benefits and potential risks, such as air pollution, public health issues, and policy transparency. Traditional sentiment analysis only shows general positive or negative opinions and cannot reveal detailed views across different aspects like the environment, policy, health, and economics.

approach.title: Data Collection
approach.text: Tweets collected via Playwright based scraping by monitoring XHR requests from Twitter's SearchTimeline endpoint using keywords: PLTSa, incinerator, PSEL, waste-to-energy.

approach.title: Zero-Shot ABSA
approach.text: Applied mDeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-xnli for aspect and sentiment classification without task-specific training data.

approach.title: Aspect Classification
approach.text: Sentiment classified across six aspects: environment & pollution, government policy, energy & electricity, public health, economics & cost, and social acceptance.

result: 75% accuracy for aspect classification, 80% for sentiment (n=102)
Environmental concerns (42.8%) and government policy (31.2%) dominate discourse
Nearly polarized sentiment: 49.7% negative vs 47.3% positive
Public health shows highest negative ratio (72.7%)
Sentiment shifts correlate with major policy announcements

title: Education Disparity Research
subtitle: Clustering of Junior High School Education in West Java

desc.overview: Analyzing regional disparities in junior high school education across West Java Province using 2024 data from the Indonesian Ministry of Education (Kemendikdasmen), combining statistical and machine learning approaches.
desc.problem: Inequality in education across regions has many aspects, including the number of schools, teacher availability, and dropout rates. Using only one indicator is not enough to fully understand educational inequality.

approach.title: Quartile Analysis
approach.text: Describes distribution of individual indicators: student-school ratio, student-teacher ratio, and dropout rate.

approach.title: K-Means Clustering
approach.text: Identifies latent regional patterns using StandardScaler normalization and multiple initializations for stability.

approach.title: Geographic Visualization
approach.text: District-level mapping using GeoPandas and Folium based on GeoJSON boundaries.

result: 3 regional clusters identified: Balanced & Stable, High-Density Stable, and Elevated Dropout Risk
Clustering provides more holistic insights than single-variable analysis
Elevated dropout risk mostly concentrated in rural areas
Findings suggest need for differentiated education policies per cluster

desc.overview: This research proposes and evaluates a multi-source AI-driven recruitment system.
desc.problem: Traditional recruitment processes depend a lot on resumes provided by candidates and on personal judgment from recruiters.

approach.title: Resume Analysis
approach.text: Parsed and analyzed using LLaMA-3 70B via OpenRouter API with zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting.

approach.title: LinkedIn Integration
approach.text: Extracted using Selenium to evaluate profile consistency with resumes.

approach.title: Twitter Analysis
approach.text: Scraped using Playwright, analyzed with XLM-RoBERTa for sentiment and behavioral indicators.

result: Cross-platform consistency checks
Behavioral insight extraction
Automated candidate summarization
Scalable across different job domains

title: Data Science Trainee Projects
subtitle: West Java Education Disparity Analysis and Clustering

desc.overview: A two-stage Data Science Trainee project that includes an early dashboard to monitor student dropout risk and a final analysis that uses clustering to study regional education patterns across West Java Province based on 2024 Ministry of Education data.
desc.problem: Education inequality in West Java varies across dropout rates, school density, and teacher availability. Effective analysis requires both descriptive monitoring tools and deeper analytical models to understand regional patterns.

approach.title: Looker Studio Dashboard
approach.text: A mid-stage output that monitors student dropout patterns across regions and education levels, helping to quickly identify areas with higher risk.

approach.title: K-Means Clustering App
approach.text: Final project built with Python and Streamlit. Users can select feature combinations, adjust cluster numbers manually or via elbow method, and explore regional groupings interactively.

result: Dashboard provides visibility into dropout distributions across West Java
3 regional clusters: Balanced & Stable, High-Density Stable, Elevated Dropout Risk
Interactive clustering app supports dynamic exploration
Both tools provide complementary descriptive and predictive perspectives

title: Undergraduate Thesis
subtitle: Sentiment Analysis of Indonesian Super Priority Destinations Using Big Data Platforms on Data Streaming

desc.overview: Undergraduate thesis developing a real-time sentiment analysis system for Indonesia's five Super Priority Destinations (Lake Toba, Borobudur, Mandalika, Labuan Bajo, Likupang) using Twitter data and big data streaming platforms.
desc.problem: Tracking public sentiment toward tourist destinations in real time is difficult because social media data is very large and fast moving. Traditional batch processing methods cannot keep up with quickly changing opinions, and limits from the Twitter API require alternative approaches for simulating and streaming data.

approach.title: Data Collection
approach.text: Tweets collected using Playwright and tweet-harvest with destination based keywords. Due to API rate limits, data was simulated as a streaming source.

approach.title: Kafka Streaming
approach.text: Collected tweets streamed second-by-second via Apache Kafka, simulating real-time ingestion into the processing pipeline.

approach.title: Spark NLP Processing
approach.text: Apache Spark handles all NLP and sentiment analysis using a dictionary-based model. Labeled results are published back to Kafka on a separate topic and sent to the Dash by Plotly.

approach.title: Real-Time Dashboard
approach.text: Dash by Plotly visualizes sentiment distribution, destination frequency, topic combinations, sentiment trends over time, and keyword analysis.

result: 61.8% neutral, 27.6% positive, 10.6% negative sentiment overall
80% of tweets assessed as tourism-relevant by expert judgment
Borobudur and Mandalika most discussed; Likupang least known
Real-time trends visualized at 1s, 10s, and 60s intervals

title: Competency Level Classifier
subtitle: Fine-Tuned FLAN-T5 for Psychometric Competency Assessment

desc.overview: A fine-tuned FLAN-T5 model developed in collaboration with a psychology department to automatically classify competency levels (1-4) from psychometric assessment responses. Focused on delivering a working end-to-end pipeline as a working solution, serving as the model component of a larger assessment system.
desc.problem: Scoring psychometric assessment responses manually can take a lot of time and may lead to inconsistent results. An automated model that classifies competency levels from psychometric assessment responses, reducing manual work and improving evaluation consistency

approach.title: Data Preparation
approach.text: Training data consists of two columns: responses (open-ended psychometric answers with dimension context merged in) and competency level labels (1-4). Labels converted to text format to match FLAN-T5's seq2seq architecture.

approach.title: Fine-Tuning FLAN-T5
approach.text: FLAN-T5 fine-tuned on the psychometric dataset to learn the mapping between response text and competency level as a text generation task.

approach.title: Collaborative Development
approach.text: Built in collaboration with a psychology program from another institution. The model was later integrated into a web-based assessment system developed by a separate team.

result: End-to-end pipeline successfully delivered, from data preprocessing to model inference
Overall accuracy: 46%; Weighted F1: 0.46 (initial baseline, not the primary focus)
Best performance on Level 1 --> Precision: 64%, Recall: 61%, F1: 0.63
Level 4 underperformed due to limited training samples (n=10)
Model successfully integrated as backend component for the web assessment system

title: RAG Document Analysis
subtitle: Document Analysis for Indonesian Banking Surveillance Report 2024

desc.overview: A RAG-based document analysis system for extracting insights from Indonesia's Banking Surveillance Report Q3 2024, combined with an interactive chatbot for question-answering against the document.
desc.problem: Large financial reports are hard to review manually. To get useful insights quickly, an intelligent system is needed that can understand the document context and answer specific questions accurately.

approach.title: Document Vectorization
approach.text: Document text converted into vector representations using sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) for fast and effective semantic search.

approach.title: Vector Search with Qdrant
approach.text: Qdrant client performs vector-based retrieval, ensuring only the most relevant document sections are surfaced for analysis.

approach.title: Chatbot via Groq + LLaMA
approach.text: Interactive chatbot powered by LLaMA-3.2-90B via Groq API, deployed with a Gradio interface for user-friendly question answering based on the report.

result: Fast retrieval of relevant sections from large financial documents
Interactive Q&A Gradio interface for the Banking Surveillance Report Q3 2024
Combined RAG + vector search enables accurate and context-aware responses
Accelerates understanding of Indonesia's banking sector conditions

title: Mutual Fund Analyzer
subtitle: AI-Powered Fund Fact Sheet Analysis with Risk Profile Personalization

desc.overview: An AI-powered chatbot for analyzing mutual fund fact sheets, personalized based on the user's selected risk profile. Built with Streamlit and powered by Gemini 2.0 Flash for document understanding and Q&A.
desc.problem: Mutual fund fact sheets contain dense financial information that is difficult to interpret for most investors. Understanding whether a fund aligns with one's risk tolerance requires financial literacy that not everyone has, making personalized AI-assisted analysis valuable.

approach.title: Risk Profile Selection
approach.text: Users select their investment risk profile (Conservative, Moderate, or Aggressive) via dropdown before starting the session, personalizing the analysis context.

approach.title: Document Upload
approach.text: Users upload a fund fact sheet PDF which is passed as context to the AI model for document-grounded analysis.

approach.title: Gemini 2.0 Flash Q&A
approach.text: Gemini 2.0 Flash processes the uploaded document and risk profile as context, enabling personalized Q&A about the fund's suitability, performance, and composition.

result: Personalized fund analysis based on Conservative, Moderate, or Aggressive risk profiles
Document-grounded Q&A, answers based strictly on uploaded fact sheet
Interactive chat UI built with Streamlit for seamless user experience
Supports analysis of any mutual fund fact sheet uploaded by the user

title: Return Shipment Prediction
subtitle: E-Commerce Product Return Prediction Using Machine Learning

desc.overview: A machine learning project that predicts the likelihood of product returns in online retail using the Data Mining Cup 2014 dataset. The goal is to help retailers reduce return rates and gain a competitive advantage.
desc.problem: Product returns are a major cost in online retail, accounting for around half of all orders. Predicting return likelihood using historical purchase and shipping data allows businesses to take action before returns happen.

approach.title: Preprocessing & EDA
approach.text: Data cleaning, handling missing values, feature engineering, and exploratory analysis on purchase and shipping attributes.

approach.title: Model Training
approach.text: Four algorithms compared: Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost. Focus metric is Recall to minimize missed return predictions.

approach.title: Evaluation & Cross Validation
approach.text: Models evaluated on Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1. 5-fold cross validation applied to assess generalization.

approach.title: Final Prediction
approach.text: Best model (XGBoost) used to predict return probability on new unlabeled purchase data.

result: XGBoost best performer --> Recall: 63.8%, Accuracy: 62.1%, F1: 61.8%
Random Forest runner-up --> Recall: 61.9%, F1: 59.3%
Naive Bayes lowest Recall (46.2%), least suitable for this use case
5-fold cross validation mean accuracy: 48.4% (±4.2%), indicates generalization challenge on unseen data
XGBoost selected as final model for unlabeled data prediction
